children: Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - September 1, 2026) - Apptly Health Technologies Corp.
(FSE: 4KL)
(the "
Company
" or "
Apptly
"), operator of the UberDoc direct-pay healthcare marketplace, today announced a strategic partnership with Koning Corporation ("
Koning
"), manufacturer of the FDA-approved Koning Vera Breast CT.
Highlights:
FDA-Approved Breast CT:
The Koning Vera Breast CT is the only breast CT system with FDA premarket approval for diagnostic imaging of the breast.
Market Access Model:
Koning gains direct reach to patients already searching for care and ready to pay, while UberDoc adds imaging sites to its marketplace at transparent, upfront prices.
Clinical Need:

Mammography may miss an estimated 10-30% of breast cancers per the National Cancer Institute, rising to as much as 70% in women with extremely dense breast tissue per the American College of Radiology.
Proven Technology at Scale:
Koning Vera systems are installed in six countries and have been used to image more than 200,000 patients worldwide.

The partnership is built around market access. Koning has spent more than a decade proving the clinical case for breast CT and placing systems in the field. What has been harder is closing the distance between a patient who needs the study, and a site that has the system. UberDoc solves for that distance directly: patients search, see the price, and book, without a referral and without a payer contract standing in the way.

Under the agreement, Koning will display UberDoc physician and service listings within its platform and introduce its provider sites to UberDoc with the goal of onboarding them to the marketplace. Apptly, through UberDoc, will supply physician and service data along with trackable links that allow patients on Koning's platform to move directly into UberDoc to find and book an appointment. The companies will run joint marketing activity and will scope potential technology integrations for cash pay appointments over the course of the term.

For patients, the effect is a shorter path between learning that advanced breast imaging exists and being able to schedule it. More specifically, a woman whose mammogram returns an inconclusive or difficult-to-read result by the clinician, particularly a woman with dense breast tissue, often faces a sequence of authorizations and unexplained costs before she reaches a next-step imaging study. With UberDoc, she can see which physicians offer the study, what it costs, and when appointments are available.

The clinical need is well documented. According to the National Cancer Institute, mammography may not detect between ten and thirty percent of breast cancers, with misses frequently attributed to high breast density or fast-growing interval cancers. The American College of Radiology reports that for women with extremely dense breast tissue, up to seventy percent of cancers may go undetected by mammography alone.
The Koning Vera Breast CT is indicated to provide three-dimensional images for diagnostic imaging of the breast and is intended to be read alongside standard two-view mammography.

"Every physician has had the conversation where a patient is told her mammogram was inconclusive and that she needs further imaging, and then watches her disappear into a maze of authorizations. Some of those women never come back," said
Dr. Paula M. Muto

, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the Company. "The constraint in specialty care is almost never demand. It is discovery, and it is price opacity. A patient cannot find the physician who has the equipment, and when she does find her, she cannot find out what it costs until after the fact. Koning built a device that gives radiologists a genuine three-dimensional look at the tissue without compressing it, and it is FDA approved for diagnostic use. Our job is to make sure a woman can find the physician who offers it, see what it costs before she commits, and get on the schedule this week rather than next quarter."
"We have spent more than a decade building the clinical evidence for breast CT and putting systems into the field across 6 countries and around 40 locations globally," said
David Georges

, North America President, Koning. "The constraint has never been whether the technology works. It has been the distance between a patient who needs this study and a site that has the system. UberDoc gives our provider sites direct reach to patients who are actively looking and ready to book, without waiting for a payer contract to be negotiated first. Putting a device with a real clinical differentiator inside a marketplace where the price is visible before the booking is a market access answer to an adoption problem, and it is a meaningful addition to how we bring this technology to the people it was built for."
Agreement Terms

The agreement is for an initial term of twelve months from the effective date and renews for successive twelve-month terms unless either party provides written notice before the end of the then-current term. Either party may terminate for convenience during a renewal term on 60 days notice, or at any time for an uncured material breach. The parties have acknowledged their intent to establish a commercially reasonable revenue-sharing arrangement for transactions generated through the collaboration; the methodology, payment terms and any applicable exclusions have not yet been agreed and would be documented in a separate written amendment. The Company has not attributed any revenue to the agreement and no assurance can be given that a revenue-sharing arrangement will be concluded.
About Apptly Health Technologies Corp.

Apptly Health Technologies Corp. operates UberDoc, a direct-pay healthcare marketplace that connects patients directly with board-certified specialists through transparent, upfront pricing. The platform eliminates traditional referral requirements and insurance barriers while providing faster access to specialty care. With more than 5,000 specialist physicians and clinicians across more than 55 specialties in all 50 states, the platform enables patients to access timely care while helping physicians expand patient access and grow their practices. The Company was founded by Dr. Paula M. Muto, MD, FACS.
About Koning

Koning is a global health technology company focused on advancing breast imaging through its patented Koning Vera Breast CT. Koning Vera holds FDA premarket approval for diagnostic imaging of the breast and for 3D-guided biopsy, and produces true three-dimensional images without breast compression at radiation dose levels comparable to diagnostic mammography.
